subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should OpenClaw solve this as a narrow per-job/heartbeat elevated authority marker, or fold elevated exec authority into the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design?
rationale: The answer determines the persisted cron/API shape, heartbeat trust semantics, execution-time checks, audit trail, and upgrade behavior for host-elevated exec authority.

options.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
options.body: Treat elevated-exec authority as a required part of the broader schedule provenance model while keeping heartbeat provenance explicitly in scope.

options.title: Implement Narrow Elevated Markers
options.body: Add a focused per-job elevated flag and heartbeat modifier provenance with create, update, execution, migration, and docs coverage.

options.title: Fail Closed For Internal Sources
options.body: Remove cron-event and heartbeat wildcard elevation only if maintainers accept the compatibility break and provide recovery guidance.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
recommendation.body: Treat elevated-exec authority as a required part of the broader schedule provenance model while keeping heartbeat provenance explicitly in scope.

likelyOwner.reason: PR 96883 is the closest recent owner path for scheduling identity and cron authority decisions.
